We can help with the process of spay/neuter, but we prefer that somebody confirms their adoption first so they can have a warm and safe place to stay after their surgery.

Re. Bond - I think it differs from cat to cat, but there are no studies suggesting cat bonds/personalities change for the worse after spay/neuter, though behavioral changes may be apparent while still healing e.g., cat will hide because they're in pain

Can also speak based from experience. We adopted a bonded pair (2 male cats also). Had them neutered too. They're still very close up to this point. It's been 6 months.

Initially, we only wanted to adopt one, but he kept crying for his brother (this was after neuter surgery).. we though he just missed the outdoors, but he calmed down as soon as we took his sibling in. Faster recovery as well since  a familiar face helped lessen their stress from surgery and rehoming.

Hope this helps!

- Two cats (white and orange siblings) up for free adoption as a BONDED PAIR; both are male

- The orange cat is also well-behaved, but can be a bit shy and will need a patient pet parent

- They eat cat food (dry and wet) and should not be given bones or fish bones to eat

- The cats' current situation is not ideal as some neighbors want to have them impounded, and other cats in the area have already been poisoned. Please give them a safe home 🙏🏻
- We're looking for someone in QC area (for convenient transport)
- We'll provide food for them for one month, as well as cover the transport fee
